extracted.intended_audience: organizations, investigators, and businesses preparing white papers, proposals, grants, contracts, or other submissions in response to ONR BAA N00014-24-B001
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation / administrative requirements for preparing and submitting white papers, full proposals, and award-related documentation to the Office of Naval Research under BAA N00014-24-B001. Covers evaluation process, compliance (export, human/animal/biosafety), subcontracting, proposal format, and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative importance of evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria 1, 2, and 3 are equally important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three evaluation criteria (as stated elsewhere in the BAA) carry equal weight in the review/selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation not head-to-head
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will not be evaluated against each other since they are not submitted in accordance with a common work statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR intends to review all proposals as soon as possible but may review periodically for administrative reasons. Selection recommendations are made by ONR's scientific/technical community; forwarding a proposal for award does not guarantee funding (cost analysis, responsibility determination, funds availability and other steps follow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced cybersecurity compliance may be required prior to award
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, certain offerors may be required to demonstrate compliance/the ability to comply with enhanced cybersecurity requirements prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Appendix 2, Section F, Part 2, Administrative and National Policy Requirements, paragraph (9) of this BAA for details. Demonstration of cybersecurity compliance can be a condition precedent to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to small business and socio-economic participation (contract awards only)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is strongly committed to providing meaningful prime and subcontracting opportunities for small businesses and socio-economically categorized firms (SDBs, WOSBs, HUBZone, VOSB, SDVOSB), HBCUs/MIs, and other concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should maximize practicable participation of these firms consistent with efficient performance; ONR provides resources (Apex Accelerators, DSBS, SAM, SBA Subnet, etc.) to assist participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan requirement for contracts over $750,000
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed contract awards exceeding $750,000, large businesses and non-profits shall provide a Subcontracting Plan containing all elements required by FAR 19.704, FAR 52.219-9, and DFARS 252.219-7003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses are exempt. The Plan must be attached to the Proposal Checklist (not included in page count). If the company has a Master/Individual or Comprehensive plan, submit a copy. Plans are reviewed for adequacy; failure to negotiate an acceptable Plan when required makes an apparent successful offeror ineligible for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan goals and explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors shall propose realistic goals to ensure small business participation to the maximum extent practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed goals do not contain positive goals, or SDB goals are below 5%, the Plan must include a viable written explanation why small businesses cannot be utilized and what attempts were made to provide opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of subcontracting resources and notice authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors may use listed resources (DSBS, SAM opportunities, Navy SBIR/STTR search, SBA Subnet, USAspending, DAU SB COP, DefenseLink, etc.) and, per FAR 5.206, certain entities may post notices to SAM to seek subcontract competition and increase small business participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must describe the business opportunity, any prequalification requirements, and where to obtain technical data needed to respond. Entities that may post include contractors awarded contracts likely to result in subcontracts and subcontractors/suppliers with subcontracting opportunities exceeding $15,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONR facilitation of subcontracting arrangements (information posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR may post contact information of small businesses that have indicated subcontracting interests and technological niche for prime contractor consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This posting is not an endorsement. Small businesses interested in being listed should provide specific contact and technology information (company name/website, POC, size/socioeconomic category, brief tech description ≤3 sentences, technology keywords ≤10) via email. Do not include proprietary information; posted information will be public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will evaluate options for award purposes by adding the total cost for all options to the total cost for the basic requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise the options during contract or grant performance. The Government reserves the right to exercise options at time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation panel confidentiality and use of support contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers and technical and cost proposals will be protected from unauthorized disclosure per FAR 3.104-4 and 15.207.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cognizant Program Officer and Government scientific experts perform evaluations; support contractors may be used for administrative purposes or as subject-matter experts but selection/award decisions are solely Government responsibility. Support contractor employees with access must sign ONR NDA for Contractor Support (including third-party beneficiary language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Award Notices and post-selection documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants receive notification email advising selection recommendation or not. Applicants recommended for award may be contacted for additional award information (representations and certifications, revised budgets, certificate of current cost or pricing data, subcontracting plan, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification email is not authorization to commit or expend funds. No funding obligation until an award document is signed by a Government Contracting Officer, Agreements Officer, or Grants Officer. Only a signed award document authorizes project commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export control compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors are responsible for ensuring compliance with all U.S. export control laws and regulations, including ITAR (22 CFR 120–130) and EAR (15 CFR 730–774), and must address in their proposals whether ITAR or EAR restrictions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors are responsible for obtaining any required licenses, approvals, or exemptions for exports of hardware, technical data, software (including deemed exports), or technical assistance. Relevant regulations and guidance URLs are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security classification identification
rubrics_metrics.description: If access to classified material will be required during performance, the Offeror must clearly identify such need in Section II, Block 11 of the Proposal Checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classified access is required, a DD Form 254 will be attached to the award and FAR 52.204-2 will be incorporated. ONR does not provide access to classified material under grants or cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for use of animals in research
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must follow DoD Instruction 3216.01 and related implementing instructions. If animals are to be used, submit a Full Appendix or Abbreviated Appendix with supporting documentation (IACUC approval, IACUC approved protocol, most recent USDA inspection report) prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact ONR Animal Use Administrator for assistance and follow provided guidance URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for human subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must protect rights/welfare of human subjects and comply with the Common Rule at 32 CFR part 219, DoD Instruction 3216.02, SECNAVINST 3900.39E Change 1, 10 U.S.C. 980, and FDA/other laws as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to award, submit IRB approval (protocol, informed consent, IRB materials and registration), proof of completed human research training for PI/co-investigators/support personnel, and institution's DHHS Federal Wide Assurance (FWA). For claimed exemptions, submit documentation including category and rationale signed by IRB Chair or designee. Documentation must be submitted to ONR HRPO via Program Officer; HRPO retains final judgment and research must not commence until HRPO has approved and Contracting/Grants Officer notifies awardee. Work performed in violation will not be reimbursed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and biosecurity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must comply with DODM 6055.18 and at least the minimum applicable requirements of CDC's BMBL and NIH Guidelines, and any applicable FDA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure laboratory biosafety standards are met; follow current editions and applicable agency guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for research involving rDNA / synthetic nucleic acid molecules
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must not begin performance of NIH-Guidelines-scope rDNA research until ONR has reviewed and accepted the Offeror’s documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a written institutional statement of compliance (on letterhead, by an official other than PI), evidence of IBC approval or determination of exemption, and DHHS letter of IBC compliance or latest DHHS compliance letter. Contact ONR HRPO for assistance, especially for work outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions and USG funding agencies subject to the USG Policy for Institutional Oversight of Life Sciences Dual Use Research of Concern must comply with all listed requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposals involve certain biological agents or toxins, contact the cognizant Technical Point of Contact. Refer to S3 dual-use guidance URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD High Performance Computing Program (HPCMP) access
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees of ONR contracts, grants, and other instruments may be eligible to use HPCMP assets if ONR Program Officer approval is obtained and security/screening requirements are completed favorably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult HPCMP website for more information and coordinate with Program Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project and Program Review Meeting expectations and cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Review Meetings between ONR sponsor and performer may be held as necessary (typically two in-person per year; additional meetings via teleconference/web). Program Review Meetings are generally held once per year (2-3 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cost estimating assume 40% of review meetings at or near ONR Arlington VA and 60% at other facilities within the continental U.S. Offerors may offer use of their facilities for Program Review Meetings with a specified offer statement; including such language will not affect selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTS UAS acquisition and operations restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial Off-The-Shelf Unmanned Aircraft Systems (COTS UAS) may not be purchased for prototype under this award until a Cyber Exception to Policy (ETP) is obtained by the cognizant ONR Program Officer, except in specified campus/basic research grant cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: Cyber ETP not required when research is via grant, unclassified, funded with basic (6.1) or applied (6.2) research funds and performed on campus by a university. Cyber ETP is required for all efforts interacting with military personnel, DoD property or facilities, USG labs/UARCs/FFRDCs, PAO, classified, or exploring military utility. Prospective performers must notify Program Officer of anticipated COTS UAS purchases at time of white paper/proposal submission or award changes and provide documentation (type of drone, effort, location). Performers must cooperate in cyber vulnerability assessments and other requirements. NDAA Section 848 restrictions (and later amendments) may apply effective Oct 1, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements references
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting requirements differ by award instrument; see Appendix 1 for Grants/Cooperative Agreements and Appendix 2 for Contracts and Other Transaction Agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must follow the specific reporting instructions in the applicable appendix for post-award reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications protocol for questions
rubrics_metrics.description: All UNCLASSIFIED communications shall be submitted via e-mail to the Technical POC with a copy to the designated Business POC. CLASSIFIED questions must follow a defined secure process—do not email classified questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ask a classified question, send an UNCLASSIFIED email to the ONR Security POC with copies to Technical and Business POCs stating desire to ask a classified question; the Security POC will arrange secure communication. Specific technical/business/security POCs and contact emails are provided for topic areas (including MCWL and ONR Global).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal file format and technical constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Files attached to mandatory forms must be PDF, must not contain macros, and must not be password protected; file names must not exceed 68 characters including extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an attachment violates these rules, it will not pass ONR’s automated acceptance check and will be rejected. Resubmissions must be marked 'New' in SF 424 Block 2 'Type of Application'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal typography and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Full Proposal Format requires single spacing and Times New Roman font no smaller than 12 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss page limits for the Technical Proposal with the cognizant Program Officer. There are no page limitations for the Budget. The Program Officer may provide specific page limits for technical sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424 and R&R forms mandatory use and field-specific instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The SF-424 (R&R) form must be used as the cover page; mandatory R&R family forms are required. Complete fields per pop-up instructions and the BAA's specific guidance for certain fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key field instructions provided (e.g., Field 3 leave blank; Field 4a new proposals enter N00014; Field 4b enter 3-digit Program Office Code with Program Officer name in brackets; add leading zero to two-digit codes; use Code 600 for ONRG; Field 5 email used for EDA profile; Field 7 list White Paper Tracking Number if applicable; Field 16 choose 'No' for E.O. 12372; Field 17 certifications and agreement language; Field 19 Authorized Representative email must match signer or submit letter of authorization). Failure to provide Program Officer Code may result in rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project summary/abstract content and format restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Project summary/abstract must identify research problem and objectives, technical approaches, anticipated outcome if successful, and impact on DoD capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only characters on a standard QWERTY keyboard; spell out Greek letters and non-English letters/symbols; graphics are not allowed; one page or 4,000-character limit (whichever is less). Do not include proprietary/confidential information; the abstract must be marked 'Approved for Public Release' and will be posted publicly on the DTIC website.

rubrics_metrics.name: R&R Other Project Information field completion (human subjects, vertebrate animals, environmental)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must address Human Subject Use (Fields 1/1a), Vertebrate Animal Use (Fields 2/2a), and Environmental Compliance (Fields 4a–4d) on the R&R Other Project Information form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For human subjects/animals, follow the BAA Section F submission requirements prior to award. For environmental compliance, briefly indicate whether research will result in environmental impacts outside the laboratory and how compliance will be ensured. NEPA considerations may apply; most basic/applied lab research is often categorically excluded, but refer NEPA questions to technical POC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract field handling in SF-424 (Field 7 instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave Field 7 blank on the R&R form; complete Form SF424 Project Abstract. If an error occurs when leaving Block 7 blank, upload the Project Abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the procedural workaround if the system flags an error for blank Block 7.
